note: Lever 4c. As lever 2 with the presence penalty of 1.5 that the model file sets by default turned off (the bridge does not send it).

items.text: 黛玉冷笑道：「我就知道，別人不挑剩下的也不給我。」
items.answer: Daiyu sneered, "I knew it. No one else gets the leftovers, and they give them to me."

errors.evidence: No one else gets the leftovers, and they give them to me.
errors.why: The conditional double negation (they'd only give me what others had passed over) is misread, so the idea that the others chose first and Daiyu gets what they rejected is lost.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: "Every day I tell you that you are too weak; how can you let the people in the house get away with this?"

errors.evidence: how can you let the people in the house get away with this?
errors.why: The rhetorical 還了得了 ('this is intolerable') becomes a direct question aimed at the addressee, which slightly shifts the force; the meaning is still close.

errors.evidence: the people in the house
errors.why: 家裡人 means household servants; this wording is vague, though context still lets the reader understand.

items.text: 寶玉未及回言，只見舡頭上來了兩人，一僧一道，夾住寶玉說道：「俗緣已畢，還不快走。」
items.answer: Before Baoyu could reply, two figures appeared at the bow of the boat—one a monk, the other a Taoist priest. They stepped forward, flanking Baoyu, and said, "Your mortal ties are now complete; why do you not hasten to leave?"

items.text: 平兒笑道：「『得饒人處且饒人』，得省的將就些事也罷了。
items.answer: Ping'er smiled and said, "Where it is possible to let people off, one should spare them; let's just make do with what we can save."

errors.evidence: let's just make do with what we can save
errors.why: 得省的將就些事 means to save trouble and let matters pass, not to make do with what can be saved; this is the material-sense trap.

errors.evidence: let's just make do with what we can save.
errors.why: The mild sense of 也罷了 (it would be fine/best to let things pass) and the word 事 (matters) are lost.

items.text: 黛玉道：「不曾讀，只上了一年學，些須認得幾個字。」
items.answer: "I have not studied; I have only attended school for a year and can recognize a few characters."

items.text: 因此劉姥姥看不過，乃勸道：「姑爺，你別嗔著我多嘴。
items.answer: That was why Aunt Liu, unable to bear it, advised him, saying, "Young master, don't be angry with me for speaking my mind.

errors.evidence: Young master
errors.why: 姑爺 means son-in-law, here a mother-in-law addressing her daughter's husband; "Young master" misrenders the relationship.

errors.evidence: Aunt Liu
errors.why: 姥姥 is better rendered "Granny Liu" or "Old Mrs. Liu"; "Aunt" is an inexact title.

errors.evidence: for speaking my mind
errors.why: 多嘴 means talking out of turn or butting in, not frankly speaking one's mind; the apologetic nuance is shifted.

items.text: 李貴笑道：“不怕你老人家惱我，素日你老人家到底有些不正經，所以這些兄弟才不聽。
items.answer: Li Gui smiled and said, "I dare not fear your displeasure, my lord. You have always been a bit undisciplined, which is why these brothers do not listen to you."

errors.evidence: I dare not fear your displeasure, my lord.
errors.why: The polite preface 'don't be angry with me for saying so' is muddled into an odd 'I dare not fear', though the apologetic gist is partly kept.

errors.evidence: You have always been a bit undisciplined
errors.why: '不正經' means improper or not upright in conduct, not 'undisciplined'; the frank rebuke is slightly shifted.

errors.evidence: these brothers do not listen to you
errors.why: 'Brothers' is unclear for the young schoolmates; 'young fellows' or 'cousins' would read more naturally.

items.text: 作者自云：因曾歷過一番夢幻之後，故將真事隱去，而借通靈之說，撰此《石頭記》一書也。
items.answer: The author says: Having once experienced a dream and an illusion, he has hidden the true events and, by means of the tale of the Spirit of the Jade, composed this book, The Story of the Stone.

errors.evidence: by means of the tale of the Spirit of the Jade
errors.why: 通靈 refers to the jade/stone being spiritually aware (magic jade of spiritual communication); "Spirit of the Jade" is inexact but close.

errors.evidence: Having once experienced a dream and an illusion
errors.why: 夢幻 is one compound meaning a dream-like illusion, and 一番 means a spell; splitting it into "a dream and an illusion" is slightly off.

items.text: 孫悟空在傍聞講，喜得他抓耳撓腮，眉花眼笑，忍不住手之舞之，足之蹈之。
items.answer: Sun Wukong listened to the sermon from the side, so delighted that he tweaked his ears and scratched his cheeks, his brows bloomed and his eyes smiled, unable to restrain himself from dancing with his hands and stamping with his feet.

items.text: 有一般天罡數，該三十六般變化；有一般地煞數，該七十二般變化。
items.answer: There is the Celestial Star number, which entails thirty-six transformations; there is the Earthly Fiend number, which entails seventy-two transformations.

items.text: 悟空道：「我自聞道之後，有七十二般地煞變化之功，觔斗雲有莫大的神通；善能隱身遯身，起法攝法。
items.answer: Wukong said, "Since I heard the Way, I have mastered the seventy-two transformations of the earth and the great power of the Somersault Cloud; I am skilled in hiding my body and vanishing, and in casting spells and commanding the laws.

errors.evidence: commanding the laws
errors.why: 攝法 means drawing in or controlling magic, not commanding "laws"; the legal sense of 法 is wrong, though casting spells nearby softens it.

errors.evidence: Since I heard the Way
errors.why: Awkward; "learned the Way" or "heard of the Way" is more natural, and the sense of studying under a master is weak.

items.text: 卻說他師徒兩個策馬前來，直至山門首觀看，果然是一座寺院。
items.answer: Now, he and his disciple rode their horses forward until they reached the mountain gate and looked on; indeed, it was a temple.

errors.evidence: he and his disciple rode their horses forward
errors.why: 他師徒兩個 means 'master and disciple, the two of them'; the candidate makes 'he' someone else's companion, which misidentifies the referent (one master, one disciple, with no separate 'he').

errors.evidence: until they reached the mountain gate
errors.why: 山門 is the temple's main gate; 'mountain gate' without clarification may mislead, though the following 'temple' softens it.

items.text: 卻說那個妖王在洞裡歡喜道：「小的們，孫行者吃了虧去了。
items.answer: Now that demon king, inside his cave, spoke with delight: "My little ones, Sun Wukong has suffered a setback and gone."

items.text: 卻說三藏自貞觀十三年九月望前三日，蒙唐王與多官送出長安關外。
items.answer: Now, it was three days before the full moon in the ninth year of the thirteenth year of Zhenguan that Tripitaka, having been escorted out of the Chang'an Pass by the Tang King and the officials, set forth.

errors.evidence: in the ninth year of the thirteenth year of Zhenguan
errors.why: This garbles the date: the source says the ninth month of Zhenguan year 13, not a 'ninth year of the thirteenth year'.

errors.evidence: the officials
errors.why: The source says 'many officials' (多官), and the quantity is lost.

errors.evidence: set forth
errors.why: The source does not say he set out here. This is only an inference from the escort, and it changes the structure from 'had been escorted' to a departure.

items.text: 孔明囑付曰：「吾受劉皇叔三顧之恩，不容不出。
items.answer: Zhuge Kongming instructed him, saying, "I have received the grace of three visits from Liu the Prince of Han; I cannot but leave."

errors.evidence: Liu the Prince of Han
errors.why: 劉皇叔 means Imperial Uncle Liu (Liu Bei), not 'Prince of Han'; this gives the wrong title and misleads the reader.

errors.evidence: I cannot but leave.
errors.why: 不出 means not coming out to serve; 'leave' loses the sense of taking office and serving, and the reader would not know what is meant.

items.text: 玄德曰：「備乃中山靖王之後；自涿郡剿戮黃巾，大小三十餘戰，頗有微功，因得除今職。」
items.answer: Xuande said, "I am a descendant of the Prince of Zhongshan Jing; since I began slaughtering the Yellow Turbans in Zhuo, I have fought in more than thirty battles of varying sizes and achieved some merit, thus earning my current post."

errors.evidence: achieved some merit
errors.why: 微功 means 'slight' or 'modest' merit; the candidate drops 微, so the humble tone is lost.

errors.evidence: the Prince of Zhongshan Jing
errors.why: The title is awkwardly ordered; 'Prince Jing of Zhongshan' is the natural English form.

errors.evidence: in Zhuo,
errors.why: 涿郡 is a commandery, and 'Zhuo' alone drops that detail.

items.text: 玄德曰：「我與民秋毫無犯，那得財物與他？」
items.answer: Xuande said, "I have not taken so much as a feather or a grain from the people; where could I possibly have any wealth to give him?"

items.text: 馬謖在山上見之，大笑曰：「彼若有命，不來圍山。」
items.answer: Ma Su, seeing this from the mountain, laughed aloud: "If he has any life left, he will not come to besiege the mountain."

errors.evidence: If he has any life left, he will not come to besiege the mountain.
errors.why: "Has any life left" slightly misrenders 有命 (if he values his life / has a destined life), though the conditional and negation are preserved.

errors.evidence: seeing this from the mountain
errors.why: "This" is vague; 之 is Sima Yi scouting ("saw him"), though the meaning is roughly intact.

items.text: 張飛性起，向玄德換了坐下馬，搶出陣來，叫曰：「我捉你不得，誓不上關！」
items.answer: Zhang Fei, his temper flaring, exchanged mounts with Xuande and charged out of the formation, shouting, "I cannot catch you, so I swear I will not retreat to the pass!"

errors.evidence: I cannot catch you, so I swear I will not retreat to the pass!
errors.why: The conditional 'if I can't capture you' is turned into a stated fact with 'so', which weakens the oath's logic.

items.text: 行到赤岸坡，見蜀兵已去遠，乃引還，顧謂眾將曰：「孔明已死，我等皆高枕無憂矣！」
items.answer: Arriving at Chi'an Slope, he saw the Shu troops had long gone, so he turned back. Turning to address his generals, he said, "Kongming is dead; we may all rest easy now!"

items.text: 武松道：「只好恁地，卻又來望哥哥。」
items.answer: "Such is fine, and I shall come to visit my brother again."

errors.evidence: "Such is fine, and I shall come to visit my brother again."
errors.why: "Such is fine" is vague and could be read as approval of the arrangement. The sense is "this much is enough; I won't drink more", so the reply to Wu Da's urging to stay is blurred.

errors.evidence: "Such is fine"
errors.why: The phrasing is stilted and unnatural in English.

items.text: 智深尋思道：「這個大寺，如何敗落的恁地？」
items.answer: Zhishen pondered, "How has this great temple fallen into such ruin?"

items.text: 魯達道：「恁地時，洒家自去便了。」
items.answer: "If that is the case, I'll just go on my own."

items.text: 宋江道：「兄弟，卻是你殺了小衙內，雖是軍師嚴令，論齒序他也是你哥哥，且看我面，與他伏個禮，我卻自拜你便了。」
items.answer: Brother, it was you who killed the young master. Though it was the strategist's strict order, by age he is your elder brother. Look at me and bow to him; I will bow to you myself.

errors.evidence: Look at me and bow to him; I will bow to you myself.
errors.why: "Look at me" is a literal rendering of 且看我面; it should be "for my sake", and the closing 便了 ("that will settle it") is not conveyed.

items.text: 酒家道：「客官，你須見我門前招旗上面明明寫道：『三碗不過岡』。」
items.answer: The innkeeper said, "Guest, you must have seen the banner above my door, which clearly reads: 'Three bowls and you cannot cross the pass.'"

items.text: 戴宗連忙回轉身來問道：「壯士素不曾拜識，如何呼喚賤名？」
items.answer: Dai Zong quickly turned around and asked, "I have never had the honor of meeting you before; what is your name?"

errors.evidence: what is your name?
errors.why: Dai Zong asks why the stranger calls out his own humble name; the candidate turns this into a request for the stranger's name, which Dai Zong asks only later.

errors.evidence: I have never had the honor of meeting you before;
errors.why: The address 壯士 and the humble self-reference 賤名 are both dropped.

items.text: 見我管待客人在此喫酒，你便與他三五升米便了，何須直來問我！」
items.answer: "See that I am entertaining guests here drinking wine; you simply give him three or five sheng of rice, why must he come straight to ask me!"

errors.evidence: why must he come straight to ask me!
errors.why: The one who comes straight to ask is the retainer (you), not the priest; the subject is wrong.

errors.evidence: See that I am entertaining guests here drinking wine; you simply give him
errors.why: Reads as an imperative and is a comma splice; 'Since you see I'm entertaining guests...' would be more natural.

items.text: 鲁镇的酒店的格局，是和别处不同的：都是当街一个曲尺形的大柜台，柜里面豫备着热水，可以随时温酒。
items.answer: The layout of the taverns in Lu Town differs from those elsewhere: each has a large counter shaped like a carpenter's square right on the street, with hot water kept inside to warm wine at any time.

errors.evidence: a large counter shaped like a carpenter's square right on the street
errors.why: 当街 means facing the street; "right on the street" slightly suggests the counter is outdoors, though the meaning is mostly intact.

errors.evidence: with hot water kept inside to warm wine at any time
errors.why: "Inside" is vague; it should be "behind the counter", and "kept ready" is missing, so the sentence is less clear.

items.text: 到了年关，掌柜取下粉板说：『孔乙己还欠十九个钱呢！』
items.answer: When the New Year approached, the shopkeeper took down the blackboard and said, "Kong Yiji still owes nineteen qian!"

errors.evidence: When the New Year approached
errors.why: This loses the sense of 年关 as the year-end debt-settling time, though the timing is roughly right.

errors.evidence: took down the blackboard
errors.why: 粉板 is a lime/chalk board for recording debts; 'blackboard' is slightly inaccurate but conveys a similar object.

errors.evidence: nineteen qian
errors.why: The untranslated unit 'qian' is unexplained for an English reader; 'coins' or 'cash' would be clearer.

items.text: 孔乙己便涨红了脸，额上的青筋条条绽出，争辩道：『窃书不能算偸……窃书！……读书人的事，能算偸么？』
items.answer: Kong Yiji turned red in the face, the veins on his forehead bulging as he argued, "Stealing books cannot be called stealing... Stealing! ... What a scholar does, how can that be called stealing?"

errors.evidence: "Stealing books cannot be called stealing... Stealing!"
errors.why: It renders 窃书 and 偸 with the same word, so the contrast between the refined 'pilfer' and the plain 'steal' is lost and the argument is nonsensical.

items.text: 又好笑，又不耐烦，懒懒的答他道：『谁要你教，不是草头底下一个来回的回字么？』
items.answer: "Who needs your teaching? Isn't it simply the character 'hui' with a grass radical on top and a 'return' underneath?"

errors.evidence: "Who needs your teaching?
errors.why: The opening clause is missing: the narrator is both amused and impatient and answers listlessly, so the mood and the speaker's identity are lost.

errors.evidence: the character 'hui' with a grass radical on top and a 'return' underneath
errors.why: The character description is muddled: 'hui' is ambiguous between 茴 and 回, and the 'come and go' sense of 回 is not conveyed.

items.text: 我的父亲允许了；我也很高兴，因为我早听到闰土这名字，而且知道他和我仿佛年纪，闰月生的，五行缺土，所以他的父亲叫他闰土。
items.answer: My father gave his consent; I was also very happy, for I had long heard the name Runtu and knew that he was about my own age, born in a leap month, with an element lacking in his fortune, so his father named him Runtu.

errors.evidence: with an element lacking in his fortune, so his father named him Runtu
errors.why: It never says the missing element is Earth (土) or that Five Elements are involved, so the 闰/土 etymology of the name is lost and the causal 'so' makes little sense.

errors.evidence: born in a leap month
errors.why: 'Leap month' is acceptable for 闰月, but without the lunar-calendar sense and the link to 闰 in the name, the etymology stays unclear.

items.text: 现在我所谓希望，不也是我自己手制的偶像么？
items.answer: Is not the hope I speak of now also an idol made by my own hands?

items.text: 我看出他话中全是毒，笑中全是刀，他们的牙齿，全是白厉厉的排着，这就是吃人的家伙。
items.answer: I saw that his words were all poison, his laughter all knives, and their teeth were all lined up menacingly white—these were the men who eat people.

errors.evidence: lined up menacingly white
errors.why: 白厉厉 means gleaming white and sharp or fierce; "menacingly white" only partly conveys the sharpness.

errors.evidence: I saw that his words were all poison
errors.why: The past tense shifts the narrator's present, certain perception into narration, which weakens the immediacy; the present "I can see" fits better.

items.text: 我也不怕；虽然不吃人，胆子却比他们还壮。
items.answer: I am not afraid; even though I do not eat people, my courage is greater than theirs.

errors.evidence: I am not afraid;
errors.why: The 也 ('also/for my part') is dropped, losing a slight link to his earlier calm.

errors.evidence: even though I do not eat people, my courage is greater than theirs
errors.why: 'Even though' and the plain comparative miss the concessive 虽然...却 and the intensifying 还 ('even bolder'); 'although ... even bolder' is more natural.

items.text: 子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？人不知而不慍，不亦君子乎？」
items.answer: The Master said, "Is it not delightful to study and then review it from time to time? Is it not joyful when friends come from afar? Is it not the mark of a gentleman to be free of resentment when others do not know him?"

errors.evidence: to study and then review it from time to time
errors.why: "From time to time" slightly blurs 時 (at due times, regularly) toward "occasionally", and "review" narrows 習, though the meaning is largely intact.

items.text: 子曰：「巧言令色，鮮矣仁。」
items.answer: The Master said, "He who is glib in his speech and wears an ingratiating expression has little of benevolence."

items.text: 子曰：「君子食無求飽，居無求安，敏於事而愼於言，就有道而正焉：可謂好學也已。」
items.error: The operation was aborted due to timeout

errors.why: The operation was aborted due to timeout

items.text: 子貢曰：「貧而無諂，富而無驕，何如？」子曰：「可也。未若貧而樂，富而好禮者也」。
items.answer: Zi Gong said, "Is it good to be poor without being obsequious and rich without being arrogant?" The Master replied, "That is acceptable, but it is not as good as being poor yet happy and rich yet fond of ritual."

items.text:
牀前明月光，疑是地上霜。
舉頭望明月，低頭思故鄉。
items.answer:
Before the bed, the bright moon's light shines,
I suspect it is frost upon the ground.
I raise my head to gaze at the bright moon,
I lower my head to think of my hometown.

items.text:
紅豆生南國，春來發幾枝。
願君多采擷，此物最相思。
items.answer:
Red beans grow in the southern land; how many branches bloom when spring comes?
I wish you would gather many; this thing is the most full of longing.

errors.evidence: this thing is the most full of longing
errors.why: Awkward English; the sense is that these beans most evoke longing, which the phrasing does not make clear.

errors.evidence: how many branches bloom when spring comes
errors.why: 發 means sprout or put forth new shoots, not 'bloom', though the question sense is kept.

items.text:
千山鳥飛絕，萬徑人蹤滅。
孤舟簑笠翁，獨釣寒江雪。
items.answer:
Birds fly from the peaks of Qianshan,
Footprints vanish from every path.
A lone boatman in a straw cloak and hat,
Alone he fishes in the snow-choked river.

errors.evidence: Birds fly from the peaks of Qianshan
errors.why: 千山 ('a thousand mountains', meaning all the mountains) is treated as a place name, Qianshan.

errors.evidence: Birds fly from the peaks
errors.why: 鳥飛絕 means no birds fly at all; the candidate says birds fly, which loses the sense of cessation and reverses the meaning.

errors.evidence: A lone boatman
errors.why: 翁 means an old man; the candidate drops his age and makes him a generic boatman.

errors.evidence: snow-choked river
errors.why: 寒江 ('cold river') is dropped, and 'snow-choked' adds a detail not in the source.
